comparison: Perfect alignment on methylation and mRNA findings (C171-C178, C207-C214, C305). Both acknowledge the disconnect between extensive methylation changes and minimal mRNA changes. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes the biological significance is unclear; peer review also rates SUPPORTED, accepting the findings as validating the rationale that mRNA doesn't always predict protein levels.

Strong agreement on mouse model evidence (C10-C11, C125-C133, C247-C250). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the baseline difference in SkMARKO mice complicates interpretation; peer review describes evidence as 'convincing' without raising this concern, suggesting slightly more confidence in the findings.

Complete agreement on adipose tissue proteomic findings (C141-C149, C151, C236). Both rate as SUPPORTED and acknowledge the modest effect sizes. OpenEval notes the interpretation of mitochondrial dysfunction is speculative; peer review accepts the findings as reported without challenging the modest differences.

Full agreement on study limitations (C332-C336). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes limitations appropriately temper interpretation; peer review confirms these align with reviewer concerns about sample size and lack of mechanistic depth. Both acknowledge transparent reporting.

Agreement on clinical characterization (C70-C77). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes small sample size and phenotypic heterogeneity as limitations; peer review accepts these baseline characteristics without challenge, treating them as standard diagnostic features.

Divergent evaluations of phosphoproteomics (C8, C134-C139, C243). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED with caveat that activity interpretations are indirect; peer review rates UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'no functional studies for the indicated proteins, phosphorylation sites,' indicating greater skepticism about functional significance.

Substantial overlap on muscle fiber and proteomic findings (C6-C7, C101-C112, C115, C237, C241). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes fiber type quantification limitations due to poor biopsy quality; peer review describes evidence as 'convincing' for decreased type I fibers without noting this limitation, suggesting stronger confidence.

Partial overlap on EA treatment proteomic changes (C182-C189). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED but questions mechanism (wound healing vs. adaptive remodeling) and notes baseline abnormalities weren't reversed; peer review rates UNCERTAIN, citing 'lack of in-depth mechanistic exploration' and acknowledging uncertainty about contraction vs. needle effects.

Agreement on clinical improvements from EA treatment (C78-C82). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed documentation with appropriate statistics; peer review accepts these as presented data without challenge.

Overlap on lipid metabolism proteomic findings (C91-C96, C98). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanistic interpretations are speculative and perilipin-1 localization relies on pig data; peer review acknowledges proteomic analysis as key contribution without raising these specific concerns.

Partial overlap on STRING enrichment analysis (C88-C90). OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, emphasizing pathway enrichment strengthens biological relevance; peer review also SUPPORTED, acknowledging proteomic methodology without specifically addressing the bioinformatic validation.

Minimal overlap on perilipin-1 and lipid findings (C4, C100). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval focuses on immunofluorescence validation of proteomic data; peer review emphasizes the novel finding of elevated extramyocellular lipids in PCOS with hyperandrogenicity.

Minimal overlap on integrative conclusions (C16-C18, C242). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, noting causal claims not supported by cross-sectional data and weak correlations; peer review rates muscle fiber findings (C17) as SUPPORTED and 'convincing,' suggesting different thresholds for causal interpretation.

Minimal overlap on mechanistic speculation (C99, C277). OpenEval rates lipid metabolism findings SUPPORTED but notes mechanistic interpretations are speculative; peer review rates these specific mechanistic claims as UNCERTAIN due to lack of functional validation, showing agreement on the speculative nature.

Single claim overlap on lack of baseline protein reversal (C200). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes this questions the mechanism of metabolic improvement; peer review treats it as honest negative finding with appropriate scientific caution.

While peer review addresses some component claims separately, no direct peer evaluation of this integrated causal conclusion was found.
